# ai-memory plugins

Marketplace plugins that connect coding agents to an
[ai-memory](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory) server you run.
Everything in this directory, and the catalogs at the repository root
(`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`), is
generated by `ai-memory render-plugins`. A test fails when the committed
files differ from the generator, so edit the templates under
`crates/ai-memory-cli/templates/plugin/` and re-render instead.

| Directory | Harness | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-code/` | Claude Code (CLI and the desktop Code tab) | `claude plugin marketplace add akitaonrails/ai-memory`, then `claude plugin install ai-memory@ai-memory` |
| `codex/` | Codex (CLI and desktop) | `codex plugin marketplace add akitaonrails/ai-memory`, then `codex plugin add ai-memory@ai-memory`, then trust the hooks in `/hooks` |

The catalogs pin each plugin to the release tag (`vX.Y.Z`), so a marketplace
add only ever installs released plugin content, never unreleased edits on a
branch.

## What a plugin runs

Each plugin holds manifests, the ai-memory routing skills, a `status` skill,
an MCP entry that runs `ai-memory mcp-bridge`, and one POSIX shell script,
`scripts/ai-memory-hook`. There is no bundled binary, no build step and no
first-run download.

The script hands each lifecycle event to the installed binary's native
`ai-memory hook` command, the same command `ai-memory install-hooks` wires.
That command applies capture policy (`ignore_paths`, allowlist mode, server
profiles) before the event is spooled or sent, and delivers it only to your
ai-memory server. The script itself sends nothing. Without the binary it
prints one line of guidance at session start and exits 0, so the agent is
never blocked.

No telemetry, and no credentials in any plugin file: hooks and the MCP bridge
use the credentials the ai-memory CLI already stores.

## The binary is installed separately

Install ai-memory once (install script, Homebrew, AUR, RPM, the Docker
wrapper, or the macOS app) and run `ai-memory setup`. `ai-memory upgrade`
updates the Claude Code plugin after replacing the binary, and `ai-memory
doctor` reports the plugin, version skew against the binary, and double
wiring with settings-file hooks.

See `docs/install.md` in the repository for the full guide.
